name: Quenby Fair Share Health Cover Act

unclear.text: Whether seasonal workers count toward the 50 FTE threshold in K3
readings: U1-a: seasonal workers count by their hours, so about 380 seasonal firms with 30-49 year-round FTE are bound
U1-b: seasonal workers are left out of the count, so those firms are not bound

a_1.text: About 135,000 full-timers at firms of 50+ FTE are offered nothing, and about 105,000 are offered less than K1 requires, so K1 binds for them.

a_2.text: Some bound firms that offer nothing now choose to offer (mainly those with higher-paid staff who value cover, given the tax exclusion).

a_3.text: Money wages are fixed in the short run by pay scales and yearly raises in at-will employment.

a_4.text: Some bound firms choose to pay the charge for at least some full-timers (all the capped firms, many mid-size low-wage firms).

a_5.text: Some firms with plans short of K1 upgrade them rather than pay.

a_6.text: Wages above the minimum can adjust over the medium horizon, as raises are set.

a_7.text: At players, for the marginal pair, cover at 30% is worth less to the worker than its cost to the employer: they could have agreed on it, with the tax exclusion, and did not.

a_8.text: Workers at payers have some alternative to bound full-time work (firms under 50, part-time work, Tarnley), so the wage does not fall by the whole charge.

a_9.text: The minimum wage binds for some workers at bound firms.

a_10.text: Some employers can reschedule jobs from 30 to 35 hours to under 30 at a cost below the per-head cost.

a_14.text: Some firms near 50 FTE value staying below the line more than the extra work.

a_15.text: Owners of firms near 50 know from January 2027 that the 2027 average decides 2028 status.

a_18.text: Revenue cannot cheaply verify reported offers, and some firms report offers not made.

a_21.text: Business values reflect expected earnings, and buyers expected the Act from its introduction.

a_23.text: Over the medium to long run, workers' alternatives to bound employment are clearly worse than employers' alternatives.

a_29.text: The $4.1 million is new general-fund money.

a_33.text: Some of the 380 seasonal firms do not offer qualifying cover to their full-timers.

q18_bound_firms_can_buy_cleaning_securit.text: Bound firms can buy cleaning, security and landscaping services from contractors with fewer than 50 FTE instead of employing full-timers.

q19_some_bound_employers_can_replace_ful.text: Some bound employers can replace full-time jobs with more part-time jobs under 30 hours.

q20_some_bound_firms_near_marisport_can_.text: Some bound firms near Marisport can move work to sites across the border in Tarnley.

q21_many_of_a_bound_firm_s_rivals_in_ret.text: Many of a bound firm's rivals in retail, food service and security are also bound, so the per-head cost is common across the market.

q22_firms_under_50_fte_compete_with_boun.text: Firms under 50 FTE compete with bound firms in retail, food service, cleaning and security.

q23_bound_employers_can_cut_other_non_wa.text: Bound employers can cut other non-wage terms, such as training and schedule flexibility, where the wage cannot fall.

q24_bound_employers_that_offer_cover_pre.text: Bound employers that offer cover prefer applicants who will decline it, such as those covered by a spouse's plan.

q25_some_bound_employers_can_recast_full.text: Some bound employers can recast full-time employees as independent contractors outside the Act's count.

q26_firms_that_already_offer_qualifying_.text: Firms that already offer qualifying cover compete for workers and customers with firms whose costs the Act raises.

q27_bound_firms_profits_are_paid_from_th.text: Bound firms' profits are paid from their earnings on full-time labour.

q28_firms_with_more_than_100_uncovered_f.text: Firms with more than 100 uncovered full-timers pay no extra charge for one more uncovered full-timer.

q29_the_cap_cuts_the_yearly_charge_of_a_.text: The cap cuts the yearly charge of a large firm with many uncovered full-timers far below $3,000 per head, to about $200 per head at 1,500 uncovered.

q30_mid_size_bound_firms_compete_for_wor.text: Mid-size bound firms compete for workers and customers with the 45 large capped chains.

q31_uncapped_bound_firms_pay_3_000_per_u.text: Uncapped bound firms pay $3,000 per uncovered full-timer while capped firms pay far less per head.

q32_firms_near_50_fte_can_buy_cleaning_s.text: Firms near 50 FTE can buy cleaning, security, landscaping and similar services from contractors with fewer than 50 FTE instead of employing staff.

q33_agency_workers_count_toward_the_agen.text: Agency workers count toward the agency's FTE, not the client firm's.

q34_firms_near_50_fte_can_take_staff_fro.text: Firms near 50 FTE can take staff from agencies instead of hiring them directly.

q35_an_employee_averaging_130_or_more_ho.text: An employee averaging 130 or more hours a month counts as one FTE however many hours are worked.

q36_some_firms_near_50_fte_can_meet_extr.text: Some firms near 50 FTE can meet extra work by longer hours from existing full-timers, paying overtime, instead of hiring.

q37_crossing_50_fte_raises_a_firm_s_labo.text: Crossing 50 FTE raises a firm's labour cost by up to $3,000 a year per uncovered full-timer.

q38_some_firms_near_50_fte_already_offer.text: Some firms near 50 FTE already offer their full-timers cover that meets K2, so crossing 50 costs them little.

q39_firms_near_50_fte_compete_with_small.text: Firms near 50 FTE compete with smaller firms for workers and customers in the same trades.

q40_an_offer_is_owed_only_from_the_first.text: An offer is owed only from the first of the month after 60 days of employment.

q41_some_seasonal_firms_can_split_a_seas.text: Some seasonal firms can split a season's work among workers each hired for under 60 days.

q42_seasonal_firms_can_take_seasonal_sta.text: Seasonal firms can take seasonal staff from agencies instead of hiring them directly.

q43_some_seasonal_firms_can_cut_their_se.text: Some seasonal firms can cut their seasonal workers' hours in 2027 to keep their average below 50 FTE.

q44_under_reading_u1_a_about_380_seasona.text: Under reading U1-a, about 380 seasonal firms with 30 to 49 year-round FTE become bound.

q45_seasonal_employers_can_cut_other_non.text: Seasonal employers can cut other non-wage terms, such as staff housing, meals or schedule flexibility, where the wage cannot fall.

q46_seasonal_employers_that_offer_cover_.text: Seasonal employers that offer cover prefer applicants who will decline it or who will leave before 60 days.

q47_some_seasonal_employers_can_recast_s.text: Some seasonal employers can recast seasonal workers as independent contractors outside the Act's count.

q48_the_minimum_wage_binds_for_some_seas.text: The minimum wage binds for some seasonal workers at these firms.

q49_seasonal_firms_profits_are_paid_from.text: Seasonal firms' profits are paid from their earnings on labour.

q50_quenby_s_farms_food_processors_and_r.text: Quenby's farms, food processors and resorts compete with producers in Tarnley, which the Act does not bind.

q51_some_of_the_380_seasonal_firms_alrea.text: Some of the 380 seasonal firms already offer qualifying cover to their full-timers, so being bound costs them little.

q52_charges_collected_under_k1_are_paid_.text: Charges collected under K1 are paid into Quenby's general fund.

q53_quenby_sets_its_other_general_fund_s.text: Quenby sets its other general-fund spending with the fund's balance in view over the budget cycle.

q54_the_indigent_care_program_s_payments.text: The Indigent Care Program's payments to hospitals are paid from Quenby's general fund.

q55_the_45_capped_firms_each_with_far_mo.text: The 45 capped firms, each with far more than 100 uncovered full-timers, would pay about $13.5 million a year under K1 if they pay the charge.

q56_the_k1_charges_paid_by_the_capped_fi.text: The K1 charges paid by the capped firms alone exceed the $4.1 million a year appropriated for enforcement.

q57_workers_whose_hours_at_a_bound_firm_.text: Workers whose hours at a bound firm are cut below 30 a week can take extra part-time work at firms under 50 FTE.

q58_bound_employers_that_cut_jobs_from_3.text: Bound employers that cut jobs from 30-35 hours to under 30 fill the lost hours by hiring more part-time workers.

q122_firms_under_50_fte_are_not_bound_by.text: Firms under 50 FTE are not bound by K1, so many of them offer no health cover.

q127_workers_who_leave_bound_full_time_j.text: Workers who leave bound full-time jobs near Marisport seek work in Tarnley.

q128_workers_who_lose_bound_full_time_jo.text: Workers who lose bound full-time jobs seek part-time jobs under 30 hours at bound firms.

q129_workers_at_bound_firms_that_pay_the.text: Workers at bound firms that pay the charge can take jobs at firms that already offer qualifying cover.

q157_firms_under_50_fte_buy_supplies_and.text: Firms under 50 FTE buy supplies and services from local suppliers in proportion to the work they do.

q160_firms_under_50_fte_compete_for_work.text: Firms under 50 FTE compete for workers and customers with the 45 large capped chains.
